---
title: Feature flags
description: Flag policy, lifecycle catalog, admin dashboard and the mobile evaluation contract.
---

The root `config/feature-flags.json` owns the mobile runtime flag inventory. Each
array entry has
`key` (unique snake_case), `description`, `owner`, `class` (`read`, `write`, `ui`,
`kill`), `default: false`, and `removeBy` (ISO date). The optional `scope` field
accepts `workspace`; workspace-scoped entries are inventory-only in the v0 mobile
endpoint and return their defaults, independently of workspace configuration.
The initial 16 mobile flags belong to `mona` and retain legacy removal-date
metadata of `2027-01-31`. Removal eligibility follows the catalog kind below.

`tutoring_parent_message_v2` belongs to `pax`, defaults OFF, and has workspace
scope. Its runtime value comes from `workspace_configs`, independently of the
v0 mobile evaluator. Only the exact string `true` enables it; setting it to
`false` or removing it is the kill switch. See
[parent message v2](/platform/applications/tutoring#parent-message-v2).

## Add a flag

Name the flag in its PR, add its registry entry with default OFF, assign an owner
and lifecycle metadata, and wire its kill switch before enabling the feature.
Follow the
[trunk-based delivery rule](/build/development-tools/git-conventions#trunk-based-delivery):
flags default OFF; kill switch first, rollback second.

Run `cd packages/feature-flags && bun run generate` after editing the JSON, then
format the generated file with Oxc and commit it. `@tuturuuu/feature-flags`
exports `registry`, the generated `FlagKey` union, and the pure
`evaluateFlags(registry, context, overrides?)` function. Its tests validate the
registry and detect generated-source drift.

## When to add a flag

Gate new features behind a flag. Routine UX/UI changes and non-critical fixes ship
without one.

## Lifecycle catalog

`config/feature-flag-catalog.json` lists every platform flag family with its
lifecycle metadata. `@tuturuuu/feature-flags` exports it as `featureFlagCatalog`
together with `getFlagLifecycle` and `validateCatalog`.

| Family | Scope | Source of truth |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `mobile-runtime` | global | `config/feature-flags.json` and the mobile endpoint |
| `workspace-secret` | workspace | Workspace secrets read through `@tuturuuu/utils/feature-flags` and Infrastructure secret definitions |
| `mobile-build` | build | Non-secret mobile deployment settings compiled with `bool.fromEnvironment` |

Each entry records `owner`, `createdAt`, `apps` (with `appsComplete` when every
consumer app is traced), `sources`, `defaults` per environment (`development`,
`staging`, `production`) and `verifiedOnProdAt`. Defaults are the declared value
when no override or workspace setting exists; they are not observed production
state.

`kind` separates removable feature flags from retained controls:

- `release` flags gate a new feature. Once `verifiedOnProdAt` is recorded,
  `removeBy` is derived as that instant plus 48 hours and the flag is overdue
  after it.
- `kill-switch`, `workspace-gate`, `safety-control` and `operational` entries are
  retained controls. Neither verification nor legacy deadline metadata makes them
  removal-due.

Entries adopted without historic metadata have `legacy: true`; their unknown owner
or creation date stays `null` and renders as unknown. For release flags only, a
`legacyRemoveBy` date is due through the end of that UTC day. New entries need
`legacy: false`, an owner,
`createdAt`, a description and a complete app list. Record `verifiedOnProdAt`
only from an actual production verification, never from defaults or CI results.

`packages/feature-flags/src/catalog.test.ts` fails when a source family gains or
loses a flag without a catalog change, when a recorded source stops naming its
flag, or when a new entry is marked legacy.

### Overdue check

`node packages/feature-flags/scripts/check-lifecycle.mjs` reports malformed
metadata and overdue flags as GitHub annotations. Cheap PR Checks runs it in
warning mode, which exits 0. `--strict` exits 1 on any report; `--now <iso>` and
`--catalog <path>` pin the clock and input.

### Dashboard

Infrastructure `/<wsId>/feature-flags` renders every catalog flag for root
workspace members with `view_infrastructure`. A root member with
`manage_workspace_roles` can override the 16 mobile-runtime registry keys per
`development`, `staging`, and `production`. The page shows the declared default
and the effective value after the `mobile_offline` master gate. Workspace-secret
flags stay read-only, with the label "Managed per workspace in Secrets" and a
link to `/<wsId>/workspaces`. Mobile-build flags stay read-only and are labeled
build-time. `cookieConsentBanner` is a separate export and is not a registry
toggle. Saved-state or audit failure stays explicit. The page does not invent a
persisted OFF value, and it does not select a workspace or write workspace
secrets.

Platform state is one row per flag key and environment. Resetting to the declared
default keeps the revision and stores an empty override. Audit is append-only.
Merging this documentation does not apply the database migration or expose the
private functions; that deployment is separate.

## Mobile endpoint

`GET /api/v1/mobile/feature-flags?wsId=<uuid>` accepts the existing session or
mobile app-session authentication. Authentication failures return 401. `wsId` is
optional; when supplied it must be a UUID (400 otherwise), and the caller must
belong to that workspace (403 otherwise). Membership lookup failures return 500.

A 200 response contains only:

```json
{
  "version": "<sha256>",
  "ttlSeconds": 30,
  "flags": { "mobile_offline": false, "offline_read_notes": false }
}
```

The example abbreviates `flags`; the response includes **every registry key**.
`version` hashes the JSON payload `{ttlSeconds, flags}` with SHA-256, excluding
`version` itself. `ETag` is that version in double quotes. A matching
`If-None-Match` returns 304 with no body, after authentication and membership
checks. Responses use `Cache-Control: private, no-cache` and
`Vary: Authorization, Cookie`. The mobile reader polls using the 30-second TTL
and retains the last payload on 304. No user or workspace identifiers are
returned. User identity comes only from the authenticated session; query
parameters cannot select a user. The handler uses
`await connection()` for request-time evaluation, with no shared output cache.
Both `CDN-Cache-Control` and `Vercel-CDN-Cache-Control` are `no-store`, including
304 and error responses.

## Evaluation

After authentication and membership, the endpoint reads platform overrides for
one server-selected environment. `VERCEL_ENV=production` selects production,
`preview` selects staging, and `development` selects development. An unknown
`VERCEL_ENV` selects production. When `VERCEL_ENV` is unset, `NODE_ENV` of
`development` or `test` selects development and every other value selects
production. A query or body field cannot select the environment.

Missing or unreachable storage uses each registry default. An authorization
failure or a malformed payload returns an error and does not substitute defaults.
The pure evaluator accepts overrides for known keys only and applies the kill
switch last: `mobile_offline: false` forces every `offline_` key OFF, including
reads, writes and status UI. Context currently has no effect on the boolean
result. This endpoint does not enable offline functionality or grant access to
underlying data.

Regression coverage lives in `packages/feature-flags/src/index.test.ts`,
`packages/feature-flags/src/{catalog,lifecycle,check-lifecycle}.test.ts`,
`apps/web/src/app/api/v1/mobile/feature-flags/route.test.ts` and the Infrastructure
`feature-flags` page and table tests.

Cookie-authenticated state mutations require the Infrastructure origin and the
`x-tuturuuu-feature-flag-action: 1` header. Bearer API requests use verified token
authentication without a cookie fallback.

## Server-side audience rules

New release flags declare rollout metadata in the central catalog: stage,
owner and a calendar-date removal deadline. Stages are internal, rollout and ga.
Internal audiences default to the exact tuturuuu.com email domain. Subdomains,
suffix matches, anonymous identities, missing emails and unconfirmed emails are
denied. Server adapters pass an actor returned by verified authentication,
including email_confirmed_at. Request JSON, query parameters, editable profile
metadata and a badge never establish that identity.

Call isFeatureEnabled(key, { user, workspace, permissionGranted }, configuration)
on the server before rendering a surface or performing its operation.
The enabledFlags configuration contains the owning evaluator's boolean results,
including its kill-switch rules. The rollouts configuration contains reviewed
catalog policies. Missing policies fail closed. The caller passes its existing
authorization result as permissionGranted; an audience never grants access.
Do not cache the result across actors or workspaces or trust a client suffix check.

An internal policy can declare emailDomainAllowlist; an empty list admits nobody.
Rollout policies select explicit workspace IDs or an integer percentage from
0 to 100. Percentage assignment is deterministic for the flag, actor and workspace;
it is a rollout decision, not a security boundary. GA retains flag and permission
gates until the owning source unit removes the flag after production verification.

The Infrastructure inventory shows configured stages, owners and removal
deadlines. Adopted entries without rollout metadata remain explicitly unknown;
the inventory does not invent verification or ownership. The existing mobile
boolean evaluator and its 16-key response remain unchanged. Each surface adopts
server-side audience enforcement in its owning source unit; a catalog policy
does not retrofit client-only or build-time consumers. Workspace-secret and
mobile-build entries remain read-only.

Regression coverage is in packages/feature-flags/src/audience.test.ts and the
Infrastructure read-model tests. Source-declared policies require no database
migration or separate global badge flag.
